delta: # Story 01 — Customer reply reopens their own resolved ticket (portal) (Story:

CRM-105)

## Prerequisites

- **CONVERSATION-1-API** must be shipped: the customer-facing reply endpoint (`POST /tickets/:
id/replies` reachable by the ticket's owner) is what this screen calls. See `api/src/features/conversation/conversation.routes.js
:16` (comment) and `api/src/features/conversation/customer-reply.test.js:1` for the API contract this WEB story cons

umes.
- **TICKETS-11-API** must be shipped: the reopen-on-reply rule (T-5) is enforced server-side. See `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.rules.js
:150` and `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.service.js:717` — the API flips `resolved → reopened` in

side the 14-day window; the screen only mirrors that.
- **Coordinate with PORTAL-3-WEB (CRM-123)** — CRM-123 owns the customer's read
view of a single ticket. Per the intake's technical hint ("This is a customer's screen and it belongs with the portal's
"), the reply UI must live inside the same route/screen CRM-123 renders (`web/src/pages/portal/PortalTicketPage.tsx`), not a separate page. Do **

not** duplicate the ticket-read logic.
- Out of scope: any `api/` change (owned by **CONVERSATION-3-API (CRM-104)**).

---

## Story

Goal

A signed-in customer viewing **their own** ticket in the portal can compose and post a reply from the same screen. The reply appears in the thread, and if
the API reopens a resolved ticket in response (T-5, 14-day window), the screen's status label updates to match.
Because a status change nobody expected reads as a fault, the screen **must** display an explicit "replying will reopen this
ticket" notice **before** the customer submits — visible whenever the ticket is `resolved` and still inside the 14-day reopen window (`resolved

_at` within 14 days of now).

Not in scope:
- Staff/agent replies (that is the desk's `ReplyBox`,

not this screen).
- API changes to reply, status, or reopen rules — those live in CRM-104.
- Internal notes (custom

er never sees or writes them).

---

## Context — Read These Files First

1. `web/src/pages/portal/PortalTicketPage.tsx` — the customer's
ticket screen. Locate the render body (imports at top include `./PortalTicketPage.css`, main component `export function PortalTicketPage()`
around line 39). The reply composer and the reopen-notice must render **inside** this component, under the th

read.
2. `web/src/pages/portal/PortalTicketPage.test.tsx` — extend this file rather than adding a new one. Match its fetch-stub pattern (fresh `

Response` per call, per L-30).
3. `web/src/pages/portal/useCustomerTicket.ts` — the four-state hook that fetches the ticket for the portal. The screen re

-fetches through this after a successful reply so the thread and status refresh.
4. `web/src/pages/tickets/ReplyBox.tsx` and `web/src/pages/tickets/useReply.ts` — **read
before reusing.** These belong to the desk's staff reply. Grep them to decide whether to reuse or write
a customer-scoped composer; if they assume a staff session or a staff-only field, write a small port
al-scoped composer instead (per the tech hint: "Read the shared sentence before reusing it" — same principle for

the hook).
5. `web/src/pages/tickets/ReplyBox.test.tsx` — pattern to follow for the composer's tests (idle/loading/success/error states via `useRequest`).
6. `web/src/shared/api/client.ts` and `web/src/shared/api/base-url.ts` — `request(path)` already prefixes `/api/v1`; the re

ply POST path is `/tickets/:id/replies`.
7. `web/src/shared/api/errors.ts` and `web/src/shared/hooks/useRequest.ts` — the four-state contract (`idle | loading | success

| error`) and the error shape (`fields` on error). Do not invent a second shape.
8. `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `
web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` — add every new string to **both** in the same edit. Nested objects one
level deep, camelCase leaves. Look at the existing `portal.*` group for structure; if none exists for reply, add `

portal.reply.*`.
9. `web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts` and `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` — will fail if a key is missing in one language or a literal appears

in JSX (including separators typed between tags). Per BR-6.
10. `web/src/pages/tickets/history-sentence.ts` — reference for U+2068 … U+2069 bidi
isolates around interpolated values (dates, ticket ids). If the reopen-notice interpolates the reopen deadline, wrap it the

11. `web/src/testing/stub-me.ts` — anything that mounts the desk shell must stub `/me`. The portal screen itself is customer-sc

oped, but the test harness pattern here shows how to seed the signed-in user.
12. `web/src/app/routes.tsx` (around line 134, `<PortalTicket
Page />`) — confirm the route is already wired. If the reply UI is a sibling route, wire it here;

if it lives inside `PortalTicketPage`, no route change is needed.
13. `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.rules.js` around line 150 and `api/src/features/tickets/
tickets.service.js` around line 717 — read the T-5 window definition (14 days from `resolved_at`) to compute the "inside the window" check on the client
from the fields the ticket payload already returns (do **not** re-implement cl

ock rules; mirror what the API sends).
14. `api/src/features/conversation/customer-reply.test.js` — the ground truth for the customer reply endpoint's happ
y path, refusal codes, and post-reply ticket status. The screen's error map and

post-success refetch must line up with this.
15. `scripts/criteria/conversation.md` around line 167 (

section **CONVERSATION-3-WEB**) — the four acceptance criteria this plan implements.

versation/` and `.squad/plans/portal/` (if present) — match the numbering and structure of the most recent WEB story in

the same feature.

---

## Product rules (from story)

- **T-5 (owned here on the WEB side of the guarantee):** a customer's
reply to a **resolved** ticket **reopens** it, provided the reply is submitted **within 14 days of `resolved_at`**. The reopen itself is server-authoritative; the screen must

(a) warn before the click and (b) reflect the new status after the click.
- **BR-6:** every user-vis

ible string comes from `en.ts` **and** `ar.ts`, added in the same edit.

---

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Add the

reply composer to the portal ticket screen

**File:** `web/src/pages/portal/PortalTicketPage.tsx`

- Below the existing thread render, add a composer region vis
ible only when the current viewer is the ticket's owner (the endpoint enforces this; the UI simply does not render the composer for a

ticket the viewer does not own — never show a control that will 404).
- Composer contents:
  - A `<text
area>` bound to local state. **No** `required`, `pattern`, `minLength`, or `maxLength` HTML attributes — the

API owns the rule (L-55). Trim client-side only to decide whether the submit button is enabled.
  - A submit `

<button>` labelled from `t.portal.reply.submit`.
  - A four-state area under the button that reads from the re

ply hook's status:
    - `loading` → disabled button, spinner or `t.portal.reply.sending`.
    - `error` → sentence from the

code-map (see task 3).
    - `success` → clear the textarea; trigger a refetch through `useCustomerTicket` so

the thread and status re-render from the server.
- Above the composer, a **reopen notice** rendered iff `ticket.status === 'resolved'` **and** `resolved_at` is within the 14-day
window (compute against `Date.now()` using the timestamp the API already returns; do not invent a rule). Text: `t.portal.reply.reopenNotice`
. If the sentence interpolates the deadline date, wrap the interpolated value with U+2068 … U+2069 (L-51) — see `pages/tickets/history-sentence.ts` for the ex

act isolate characters.

### 2 — Add or reuse the customer reply hook

**Grep first** for `useReply`

in `web/src/pages/tickets/useReply.ts` and decide:

- **If it can be reused unchanged** (no staff-only assumptions, no

field the customer cannot send): import it here.
- **Otherwise create:** `web/src/pages/portal/useCustom
erReply.ts` — a `useRequest`-backed hook that POSTs `/tickets/:id/replies` with `{ body: string }`. Return the four-state shape (`idle | loading | success | error`)

whose `error` carries `fields` per `shared/api/errors.ts`. Do **not** invent a second shape.

Whichever path

, the composer calls the hook, and on `success` invokes the refetch exposed by `useCustomerTicket`.

### 3 — Error sentences

: read the shared map before reusing it

**File(s):** the composer's error render + `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` + `web/src/shared/

i18n/ar.ts`.

- For each refusal code the customer's reply endpoint can return (empty body, ticket not found / not owned → 404, too-long body, thro
ttled, etc. — confirm the exact set against `api/src/features/conversation/customer-reply.test.js`), check `t.errors[code]` first. **If** the shared sentence is tru
thful for a customer replying on their own ticket, use it; **if not**, add a portal-scoped override under `t.portal.reply.err

ors[code]` and prefer that.
- Per the intake's warning: two screens have already needed their own sentence (a 401 sa
ying "session ended" when it had not; a 429 saying "too many attempts" after one). Any code where the shared sentence would confuse a customer replying to

**their own** ticket gets its own entry here.

### 4 — Strings: add to both languages

**Files:** `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts`.

Add (

at minimum) the following leaves under `portal.reply` in both files:

- `submit` — button label ("Send reply" / equivalent Arabic).
- `sending` — loading label.
- `plac

eholder` — textarea placeholder.
- `reopenNotice` — the "replying will reopen this ticket" sentence, including any interpolated deadline in a bidi isolate.

- `sent` — success confirmation (optional if the refreshed thread is confirmation enough).
- `errors.<code>` — for

each refusal code the shared map does not truthfully cover.

Keys must be **identical** across the two files or `web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.

ts` fails. No literal string may live in JSX (including a separator between tags) or `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` fails.

### 5 — W

ire the way in

Confirm `web/src/app/routes.tsx` (`<PortalTicketPage />` at ~line 134) already reaches this scre
en from a link the customer can follow (per intake: "A route only its author can navigate to is a route that does not exist"). If a customer land
ing on `MyTicketsPage` (`web/src/pages/portal/MyTicketsPage.tsx`) does not have a link into `PortalTicketPage`, add one there

. No route additions are needed for the reply itself — it is part of the same screen.

### No backend changes required.

All API behaviour (
endpoint, T-5 window, reopen transition) is owned by CRM-104 / TICKETS-11-API. This

story consumes them.

---

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Resolved ticket, outside the 14-day window** → API refuses the reply. The scre
en must **not** show the reopen notice (the notice is gated on `resolved_at` being within 14 days). Error sentence: whichever code the API returns for
"too late to reopen"; if the shared `t.errors[code]` is not truthful here, add `t.portal.reply.errors[<code>]`. Enforced in `PortalTicketPage.t

sx` render guard.
- **Resolved ticket, inside the window, customer submits** → API returns success and the ticket flips to `reopened`. The scre
en refetches through `useCustomerTicket` and the status label updates from "Resolved" to "Reopened" without a full navigation. If the refetch fails,

keep the composer's success state and show a soft error — do not roll back the server change.
- **Ticket not owned by the viewer** → the end
point returns the ownership 404 (see `api/src/platform/http/staff-only.guarantee.test.js:51
`). The composer must not be rendered in the first place; if it is somehow submitted, map the 404 to a customer-truthful sentence (not the shared "not found" if that re

ads wrong for their own ticket).
- **Empty or whitespace-only body** → client-side, disable the submit button; do **not** use `required` (L-55).

If somehow submitted, the API's refusal sentence surfaces.
- **Throttled (429)** → per the intake, the shared "too many attempts" sentence may be w

rong for a customer who has typed one reply. Add a portal-scoped sentence.
- **Session expired (401)** while composing → per the intake, a 401

does not always mean "session ended". Match the sentence to what actually happened here (the customer's session, on their own ticket).
- **R
TL + interpolated deadline date** in `reopenNotice` → without U+2068 … U+2069 the date renders wrong in Arab

ic. Enforced by wrapping the interpolation, mirroring `web/src/pages/tickets/history-sentence.ts`.
- **Concurrent reply from sta
ff** → the refetch after success will pull whatever the server currently has, including any staff message posted me

anwhile. No client-side merge logic.
- **`resolved_at` missing on a resolved ticket** (should not happen, but defensive)

→ treat as **outside** the window (no reopen notice), so the sentence is never a lie.

---

## Test Plan

All new/updated tests live in `web/
`. Vitest + Testing Library. Every fetch stub returns a **fresh** `Response` per call (L-30). Any test that mounts the desk sh

ell stubs `/me` via `web/src/testing/stub-me.ts`.

1. **`web/src/pages/portal/PortalTicketPage.test.tsx` — extend:**
   1. Ren

ders the reply composer when the viewer owns an open ticket.
   2. Renders the reopen notice **only** when the ticket is `resolved` and `resolved_at` is within 14 days of the test

's frozen "now".
   3. Does **not** render the reopen notice when `resolved_at` is 15+ days ago.
   4. Submits a reply: shows loading, then on
success clears the textarea and refetches the ticket; the thread includes the new message and, for an in-window resolved ticket, the status label reflects "re

opened" from the refetch payload.
   5. On refusal (e.g. throttled 429, too-late-to-reopen), the sentence rendered is the port

al-scoped one for that code — **not** the shared default when the shared default is untrue here.
   6. Submit button is disabled for an empty/whitespace body without using a

native validator (assert no `required`/`pattern` attributes on the `<textarea>`).
2. **`web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts`** — pass

es with the new `portal.reply.*` keys added to both `en.ts` and `ar.ts`.
3. **`web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test

.ts`** — passes; no literal string in `PortalTicketPage.tsx` (including a separator typed between tags).
4. **(If a new hook is added

)** `web/src/pages/portal/useCustomerReply.test.ts` — four-state coverage (`idle → loading → success` and `idle → loading → error` with `error.fields`).
5. **Reg

ression:** `web/src/pages/tickets/ReplyBox.test.tsx` still passes unchanged (the desk composer is untouched).

---

## Verification Steps

1

. **Frontend runs:** `cd web && npm test` — all vitest suites green, including the parity and no-hardcoded-strings guards.
2. **Frontend builds (

typechecks):** `cd web && npm run build` — this runs `tsc -b && vite build`. A change only vitest has seen is not verified.
3. **
Backend regression (untouched, sanity):** `cd api && npm test` — nothing in this story changes `api/`; the suite should be

green on the same commit.
4. **No AI attribution anywhere:** `git grep -iE 'co-authored-by:
|generated by|assisted by|copilot|chatgpt|claude|anthropic|openai' --

':!scripts/'` returns nothing in the diff.
5. **Smoke (manual, optional):** run `cd api
&& npm run seed:demo` (or the project's demo seed) then `cd web && npm run dev`, sign in as the se

eded customer, open one of their tickets:
   - Open ticket → composer visible, no reopen notice.
   - Resolved ticket within 14 days → composer visible **and** reopen notice above

it.
   - Send a reply on the resolved-in-window ticket → status changes to Reopened, message appears in the thread.
   - Resolved 15+ days ago → composer either hidden or its

refusal sentence is the portal-scoped one (not the shared default, if the shared default is untrue).

---

## Done Criteria

- [ ] Given a resolved ticket **inside** the 14-day window, the port

al ticket screen shows a reopen-warning sentence **before** the customer replies.
- [ ] Given a customer's reply on their own ticket, the message

appears in the thread on success, and the visible status follows the server (Reopened when the API reopens it).
- [ ] Given a refusal, the sentence is the shared `t.errors[code

]` **only** when it is truthful here; otherwise a portal-scoped override under `t.portal.reply.errors[<code>]` is used and shown.
- [ ] Every new
user-visible string is present in **both** `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` (BR-6); `parity.test.ts` and `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts

` are green.
- [ ] No native validator (`required`, `pattern`, `min`, `max`, `type="email"`) on the reply form (L-55).
- [

] Any value interpolated into a translated sentence is wrapped in U+2068 … U+2069 (L-51).
- [ ] The reply is submitted through a `useRequest`

four-state hook whose `error` carries `fields`; no second shape invented.
- [ ] The customer has a link into the portal ticket screen from `MyTicketsPage` (or

an equivalent), so the composer is reachable.
- [ ] `cd web && npm test` and `cd web && npm run build` both pass; `cd api && npm test` still passes un

changed.
- [ ] Nothing in the diff mentions AI assistance.
